Training recruits is an incredibly challenging endeavor. Many, many factors have to be balanced. Even adding a one-hour requirement in a 6 week block can be migraine inducing. You have an extremely limited amount of time to tear down a kid and rebuild him/her into a standardized GI. And don't be deluded--retention IS an issue. If a kid drops out of the program (self-initiated elimination) or you kick him out you've lost an investment that has already cost the taxpayer probably at least $25,000 if not more. These young folks are not conscripts legally compelled to serve against their will. They're volunteers (have been since the 70s) and can/do bail out of the program if they feel abused or broken. The military NEEDS these kids to be successful in training for many reasons, not the least of which is they need new bodies in the active ranks. Basic Training methods are often tweaked/refined to find the right balance of keeping the pipeline of qualified bodies flowing and keeping standards high.
